To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the production of important cytokines by alveolar macro phages from allergic resistant (Sprague Dawley) and susceptible (Brown Norway) rat strains is different.
alveolar macro phages from Brown Norway rats are functionally distinct from those from Sprague Dawely rats.
alveolar macro phages (AM) from Brown Norway (BN) rats produce more Th 2 cytokines, such as interleukin‐ 10 (IL‐ 10) and IL‐13, than AM from Spraque Dawley (SD) rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the mechanisms involved in the development of allergic asthma in rats.
the role of AM in the development of allergic responses and the underlying mechanisms.
the functional differences in AM from Brown Norway versus Sprague Dawley rat strains, which may be related to the development of airways allergic reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the differences in cytokine profiles between Brown Norway and Sprage Dawley rat alveolar macrohages may contribute to the differences in allergic airways inflammation between these two rat strains.
AM from Brown Norway (asthma‐susceptible strain) produce more Th2 cytokines than AM from Sprage Dawley (asthma‐resistant strain) rats.

the cytokine profile of alveolar and lung macrophages from Brown Norway and SDAW rats is different, which may be one of the mechanisms that underlies the difference in susceptibility of these two rat strains to allergic airway inflammation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Brown Norway rats are more susceptible to develop airway allergic reactions due to their AM being more pro‐inflammatory, and therefore more capable of activating T‐cells and other cells involved in the allergic inflammatory process.
AM from Brown Norway rat are more effective in producing Th2‐type cytokines, whereas AM from Sprague‐Dawley rats produce more pro‐inflammatory cytokines and less Th2‐type.
the AM from Brown Norway rat are less efficient in the production of Th1 cytokines and NO, but are able to produce more Th2 cytokines, compared with AM from the Sprague Dawley strain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytokine profile of alveolar cells is important for the development of airways allergic reactions.

the different susceptibly to develop allergic reactions in the lung of Brown Norway and Spraque Dawley rats is associated with functional differences between their AM, which may be related to the production of Th2‐type cytokines.

the different susceptiblity in the development of allergic responses in Brown Norway and Sprague Dawley rats may be related to their alveolar macrohages, and that these cells may be involved in creating a Th2‐like cytokine milieu in the lung.
